correctness.rationale: In exact arithmetic the sketched minimizer exists uniquely on span{r,Ar}. Its true-residual ratio is sin(angle(r,Ar))*sqrt(1+(B21/B11)^2), with B the restricted Gram. The matrix perturbation operator bound yields |B21/B11|<=eps/sqrt(1-eps^2), and a 2x2 Gram with eigenvalues 1±eps achieves it. A direct eigenvalue-weight proof gives sin(angle)<= (kappa-1)/(kappa+1), attained by diagonal(1,kappa), r=(sqrt(kappa),1). Both attainments hold together; rational kappa=9 witnesses demonstrate threshold equality and strict growth. All kappa>=1, 0<=eps<1 checked analytically; 10556 finite numeric cases are supplementary.

value.rationale: Sketched GMRES papers explicitly distinguish sketched norm from possibly nonmonotone true residual. This result closes the quantitative necessary-and-sufficient one-step safety gap for SPD matrices and identifies a sharp condition-number/embedding boundary, with dimension-2 extremizers, rather than merely reproducing a generic convergence bound. It is a natural algorithm-design question: when can an approximate norm still guarantee actual residual descent? The finding makes no multistep convergence or typical-sketch promise.
